Citing toxic foam in the river, AAP targeted Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, while the BJP defended its clean-up efforts and hit back at the previous AAP government.

stories.title: 'Inappropriate to lecture India on democracy': Meloni ally hits back at Italian leader's BJP vote theft jibe
stories.summary: Deborah Bergamini has expressed discontent over Giacomo Filibeck's remarks on India’s electoral process. She emphasized that India has its own political institutions to handle such disputes. Filibeck’s comments occurred during the Bharat Summit 2026, where he supported the Indian Congress Party. The BJP responded by accusing the Congress of seeking foreign interference in national matters. This situation highlights ongoing tensions between Indian political factions regarding electoral integrity and foreign influence.

stories.title: 3 grenades found in polythene bag defused in J&K's Baramulla
stories.summary: Security forces defused three grenades found in a polythene bag in north Kashmir's Baramulla district, as news agency ANI reported Monday. The recovery comes days after police arrested a man and seized two hand grenades from a forest in Tangmarg. Police are investigating the source of the explosives, their intended use and possible links.

stories.title: BJP MP Ajeet Gopchade urges PM Modi to ensure representation of divyang persons in Parliament
stories.summary: Ajeet Gopchade has requested Prime Minister Narendra Modi to develop mechanisms for the representation of divyang persons. He highlighted the successful examples from other countries that facilitate this representation in legislatures. Gopchade suggested that exceptional candidates with disabilities should be considered for Rajya Sabha nominations. The Prime Minister's Office has forwarded his suggestions to relevant ministries for further action.

stories.title: 'Perfectly safe' but not 'maxed out'? Trump takes Qatar jet to Asia
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Asia on Monday aboard the aircraft gifted by Qatar, even as questions remain over its promised security upgrades. According to NBC News, the jet has received some maintenance and cosmetic improvements, but the larger overhaul remains unclear months after an Iran-related security scare forced Trump to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane.

stories.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 as company conducts internal investigation
Yemeni govt force retreats in a setback in war against Houthis
Fresh labour unrest hits Bangladesh garment sector
PM Modi to attend Asean, East Asia summits in Manila; what's on agenda
No fresh trial for Hasina in case for which she got death: Prosecutor
US air travel disruptions continue into 3rd day
Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites as ULA's Vulcan rocket fails minutes after launch
stories.summary: Amazon's planned launch of 40 satellites for its Leo internet network failed after the Vulcan rocket malfunctioned. The Vulcan rocket, operated by United Launch Alliance, experienced an anomaly 10 minutes after liftoff. This failure poses a setback for Amazon's satellite internet plans, which aim to compete with Elon Musk's Starlink. Amazon has also invested in other launch options including Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket and Arianespace.

stories.title: 'Not Cuba or Venezuela': Iran warns it will not wait for US attack before responding
stories.summary: Iran has expressed that it is ready for potential military action while discussing diplomatic avenues with the United States. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi indicated three possible scenarios: diplomatic talks, economic blockades, and military response. Tehran has set specific conditions, including ending the war and lifting economic sanctions for any agreement. The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East adds to ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Colorado jury awards $65 million, after mother killed in crash
stories.summary: A jury in Colorado awarded $65 million to the family of Megan Arneson, who was killed in 2022. Arneson died when a truck carrying an improperly loaded excavator struck an I-25 overpass. Her 10-year-old son, who was in the vehicle, witnessed the tragic incident. The truck driver and the company both bore responsibility for the accident in the court's findings.

stories.title: Palm Beach estate tied to foreclosure suit asks $32 million
stories.summary: A mansion located at 301 Plantation Road in Palm Beach is currently listed for sale at $32 million. The property has a history of foreclosure proceedings after the seller defaulted on a $22 million mortgage. This brand-new estate features over 9,000 square feet, seven bedrooms, and luxurious amenities like a double infinity-edge pool. A total of 21 luxury deals were signed in Palm Beach County during a recent week.

stories.title: Noose tightens on Bishnoi: Cops seek jail visitor logs, up security for B-town stars
Ray of hope has reached Gadchiroli this Diwali: PM
Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC
stories.summary: The Election Commission has committed to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls during the current process. No legal action will be taken against individuals for re-registering to vote through Form 6. Voters are advised to ensure their names are not listed in other constituencies before applying. Additionally, those previously removed erroneously can submit fresh forms for their names to be reinstated.

stories.title: 'No case against me anywhere,' Lalit Modi claims to TOI
stories.summary: IPL founder Lalit Modi, who left India in 2010 amid allegations of tax evasion, money laundering and proxy ownership linked to IPL, has announced he has received British citizenship. Lalit was appearing at an event at Oxford Union when he made the announcement.

stories.title: Alabama mother regains parental rights to older child; court upholds termination for younger child
stories.summary: A recent ruling by an Alabama appeals court has partially overturned a juvenile court's ruling regarding parental rights. The mother has maintained her rights to her older child but lost her rights to her younger daughter. The court underscored the necessity of evaluating the circumstances of each child individually in such matters. Meanwhile, the father's rights to both children remain revoked due to evidence of substance abuse and inadequate support.

stories.title: Lalit gets British citizenship, extradition prospects take a hit
stories.summary: Lalit Modi has announced his acquisition of British citizenship during an event at Oxford Union. While he claims to have faced threats and political persecution, he has refused to return to India. The Enforcement Directorate has ongoing investigations regarding his alleged financial misconduct linked to IPL. Previous requests for his deportation have been denied by the UK government.

stories.title: San Francisco 'Painted Lady' bought for $1.85 million now listed for $5.595 million
stories.summary: Once a forgotten Victorian gem in Noe Valley, this home was purchased at $1.85 million and thoughtfully revived, blending its charming historic features with modern amenities. Now boasting a listing price of $5.595 million, it offers five spacious bedrooms alongside a private apartment. The extensive restoration preserved its Victorian allure while ensuring necessary structural and aesthetic updates, reflecting the growing trend of revitalizing historic homes in sought-after urban areas.

stories.title: Empty Vande Bharat allowed to run 463km despite 'poor power brake'
stories.summary: An empty Vande Bharat train journeyed 463 kilometers from Hatia to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station despite brake problems. Two loco pilots had reported issues with the power brake before the journey commenced. An investigation revealed that brakes on every coach had been isolated, leading to joint brake failure. The South Eastern Railway's document indicated staff negligence in integrating the braking systems.

stories.title: Criminal killed in 5th 'encounter' in West Bengal since May
CRPF men in anti-Naxal ops diverted to Manipur
Shah hits back at Rahul, says he's defaming India at global platforms
Alabama court upholds mother's sole custody after harassment, but orders new visitation schedule
stories.summary: After sending threatening emails to his ex-wife, an Alabama father grappled with custody issues. The court granted sole custody to the mother, citing the father's harassment. Although the appeals court upheld this decision, they recognized that the father's visitation hours were excessively limited. Consequently, a reassessment of the visitation schedule was ordered, while a protection order against him remains active until March 2027.

stories.title: Alabama student Jai Varikuti's UNICEF campaign raises nearly $5,500 across six schools
Georgia woman wins $2.5m after rear-end crash leads to spinal fusion surgery
stories.summary: A woman from Georgia received a substantial $2.5 million settlement for severe neck injuries resulting from a car accident in 2023. The incident occurred when her vehicle was rear-ended while awaiting at a traffic light. Following the crash, she underwent significant medical interventions, including spinal surgery. Her legal team emphasized how these injuries drastically altered her quality of life, highlighting the profound consequences of personal injuries.

stories.title: India bucks trend, 38 institutions up in QS sustainability study
Govt healthcare spend up 3x since 2013-14 to 4.1L cr
stories.summary: Out-Of-Pocket Expense Dips But Families Still Paid 4L Cr In 2023-24

stories.title: 'Don't make me go with him': Pennsylvania father barred from contacting son, ex-partner for 3 years
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld a three-year protection order barring a father from contacting his former partner and their seven-year-old son. The mother alleged that he pushed his way into her home during a custody handoff, behaved aggressively and frightened the child, who later begged her not to send him with his father again.

stories.title: George’s Drawing Published: Prince George’s kingfisher art appears; links three generations
stories.summary: In an exclusive edition of Country Life magazine, Prince George displayed his artistic skills with a thoughtful drawing of a kingfisher. This special issue, guided by his father Prince William, emphasizes issues such as environmental awareness and family life. Through this public piece, George connects to the creative spirit of his mother, Kate Middleton, and his grandfather, King Charles III, promoting the royal family's dedication to nature and social engagement.

stories.title: Venezuelan doctor honoured after saving toddler from drowning in Georgia pool
stories.summary: Dr. Andrea Sansonnet saved one-year-old Maddox from drowning at a swimming pool in Newnan, Georgia. Her quick actions included performing CPR until he was breathing again after being underwater for about 90 seconds. On their shared birthday, the Newnan Police Department honored Dr. Sansonnet for her lifesaving efforts during the emergency. Maddox’s mother expressed gratitude for the doctor’s presence when the incident occurred.

stories.title: California mother and newborn died after discharge; jury awards $9.25m, but old law limits payout
stories.summary: Demi Dominguez tragically lost her life shortly after hospital discharge, following alarming preeclampsia symptoms. Her baby son, Malakhi De Leon, passed away soon after birth. A jury subsequently awarded $9.25 million in damages, yet limitations under California's MICRA restrict non-economic compensation. This heart-wrenching case underscores the urgent necessity for reform in medical negligence laws, as the families advocate for changes to protect others from similar tragedies.

stories.title: 12-year study finds declining elephant numbers lead to fragmented social networks
stories.summary: A study in Udawalawe National Park indicates that dwindling elephant groups result in significant social vulnerabilities. With fewer individuals, elephants transition from larger communities to smaller, more isolated factions, which impairs their capacity to nurture and feed effectively. Once a critical social threshold is exceeded, the difficulty of reversing such fragmentation intensifies.

stories.title: Charleston opens $25m memorial 11 years after church shooting killed nine Black worshippers
stories.summary: In Charleston, South Carolina, the Emanuel Nine Memorial has been unveiled, marking over a decade since the heart-wrenching shooting. Families and community figures participated in the dedication ceremony, honoring those lost in the tragic event. The memorial features peaceful benches and a beautiful fountain, designed for contemplation and remembrance. Chris Singleton emphasized its personal importance in honoring his mother's legacy.

stories.title: Congress suggests Army ‘friendly fire’ behind deaths of 2 SPOs, BJP calls it 'provocative'
stories.summary: In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces.

stories.title: Mumbai physics forum hosts online lecture by Pak N-scientist
stories.summary: Mumbai recently held an online event to honor the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. Eminent scientist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy delivered a lecture discussing Salam's contributions to physics and his life. Hoodbhoy highlighted Salam's significance as a symbol of goodwill between India and Pakistan. He mentioned Salam's lack of recognition in Pakistan due to his Ahmadiyya sect affiliation, affecting youth role models.

stories.title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype, seeks own industry
stories.summary: Kashmiri filmmakers are advocating for a shift towards regional cinema to enhance authentic storytelling and representation. They argue that Bollywood often reinforces stereotypes that misrepresent life in J&K. The current film policy is criticized for not adequately supporting local productions while favoring external filmmakers. Actors and directors are calling for collaboration among regional artists to develop a unique Kashmiri film industry, signaling a significant movement towards self-identity and cultural expression.

stories.title: Pennsylvania court rejects son's claim of missing millions from 65-property family trust
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania court has upheld the dismissal of Jacob Singer's case over alleged mismanagement of a family trust holding around 65 properties. It found that his claim of missing millions lacked sufficient financial evidence and that he had not established a right to an accounting or immediate control of the properties.

stories.title: Minting Accident: 3D tests suggest sixpence was deformed during minting; cause remains inconclusive
stories.summary: A team of researchers has thoroughly examined a distorted silver sixpence from 1834, uncovering unexpected manufacturing flaws. Through intricate 3D imaging, they revealed significant deformations and patterns that stray from regular wear. This peculiar state of the coin prompts a deeper look into the production methods of the steam-powered minting period. The analysis, combining advanced imaging and chemistry, sheds light on historical minting defects.

stories.title: An Australian railway enthusiast spent 13 years building a mini version of a 315-kilometre route
stories.summary: After 13 years of meticulous work, Peter Michalak has crafted a stunning miniature railway that faithfully mirrors the Adelaide-to-Bridgewater route. This impressive model showcases various stations across a detailed 315-kilometre stretch. Initially designed to be portable, the project has since transitioned into a permanent display rich in detail, reflecting Michalak's family history and personal ties to the railway. Efforts are ongoing to enhance this intricate layout over the next decade.

stories.title: Kishtwar BJP leader questions Shagun Parihar’s mosque claim, Muslim body seeks public apology
Humane World for Animals rescues 951 chinchillas from Ohio breeding facility in two operations
stories.summary: A breeding facility in Jenera, Ohio, was revealed to have hundreds of chinchillas in poor conditions. Federal inspections led to the discovery of severe neglect and health issues in the animals. Humane World for Animals assisted in the rescue of 951 chinchillas, which were removed in two operations. The facility's owner agreed to surrender the animals and cease operations regulated by the Animal Welfare Act.

stories.title: Launching new anti-anaemia strategy without enough evidence could waste public funds, warn experts
Punjab BJP forms manifesto, 'chargesheet' committees; Raghav Chadha, Harbhajan Singh among members
stories.summary: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon has created two vital committees. One will meticulously draft the party manifesto, while the other focuses on compiling a detailed chargesheet. Senior leaders Avinash Rai Khanna and Sunil Jakhar are at the helm, supported by a diverse range of experts, showcasing the party's commitment to thorough preparation for a strategic electoral campaign.

stories.title: South Dakota ranchers report wildlife boom after adopting satellite-guided rotational grazing
stories.summary: In South Dakota, a ranching family has harnessed the power of rotational grazing and cutting-edge virtual fencing to rejuvenate their land's biodiversity. By allowing grasslands to rest between grazing sessions, they have significantly improved plant health and restored native ecology. This approach not only boosts wildlife populations, such as diverse bird species and larger mammals, but also streamlines cattle management with reduced labor.

stories.title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh unit has refuted claims regarding a supposed list of 209 candidates. Officials described these reports as false and part of a larger scheme. They cautioned party members against believing in unverified media stories. Additionally, they clarified that the assembly election candidate selection process has yet to commence, highlighting the importance of a methodical and unified approach to such decisions.

stories.title: Prince William, Kate to meet PM Modi in Delhi during three-day India visit
'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India
stories.summary: During a recent event in Jodhpur, RSS leader Mohan Bhagwat spoke fervently about the necessity of national unity. He indicated that smaller identities can lead to societal rifts, reminiscent of colonial tactics. Emphasizing the need for individuals to set aside ego and self-interest, he illustrated his points with lessons from the Mahabharata, stressing that unity is key to overcoming challenges.

stories.title: Utah couple turns pandemic candy search into business stocked in more than 500 US stores
Kishtwar SPOs killings: BJP says Congress remarks could fuel Pakistan propaganda, seeks apology
'Won't disappoint my workers': Kumaraswamy says he will decide on Karnataka return at right time
Arunachal governor reviews security in 3 districts, pushes for faster Myanmar border fencing
stories.summary: Governor KT Parnaik held a review meeting to assess the security dynamics in Tirap, Changlang, and Longding districts. He emphasized the urgency of advancing the border fencing initiative along the Myanmar border and called for decisive steps against drug trafficking. Highlighting the importance of collaboration among security forces and local administration, the governor voiced his worries over the delays in the fencing project and the increasing drug-related cross-border issues.

stories.title: Supertanker with 2 million barrels of oil sinks after hitting mine in Strait of Hormuz
Trump slams judge’s order blocking Washington golf course renovation
Nevada rancher permanently protects 1,228 acres for sage-grouse habitat and farming
stories.summary: David Park has successfully conserved 1,228 acres of land at Desert Creek Ranch in Nevada. This effort focuses on protecting habitats for the rare Bi-State sage-grouse while allowing continued agricultural activities. A permanent conservation agreement prevents non-agricultural development and preserves the land's ecological value. Additionally, a future grant will facilitate restoration work across 350 acres to control invasive grass and support biodiversity.

stories.title: 'No place for goons': CM Adhikari's warning to criminals after encounter of Shantiniketan accused
stories.summary: In a bold statement, Suvendu Adhikari, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, sent a clear message to those involved in crime after a police encounter resulted in the death of Ratan Sheikh, a prime suspect who reportedly shot at officers during his attempted arrest. Adhikari reaffirmed that criminal activities will not be tolerated in the state. Meanwhile, the police constable injured in the incident remains in stable condition.

stories.title: Texas family's rescued bluebonnet painting sells for $112,500 at auction
Kulgam terror attack: Search operation launched in J&K to hunt terrorists who attacked CRPF post
After 46 years, Oklahoma food bank serves its billionth meal; Thunder adds $25,000 donation
stories.summary: On November 10, the Regional Food Bank of Oklahoma marked a historic milestone by packaging its one billionth meal, a testament to 46 years of tireless support from community partners and volunteers. The Oklahoma City Thunder made a significant donation to amplify hunger relief efforts. However, food insecurity still poses a critical challenge in Oklahoma, particularly affecting children.

stories.title: US State Secretary Marco Rubio blames Iran’s ‘expansionist mentality’ for conflicts across Middle East
Punjab polls: Sukhbir Badal to take final call on alliance, says SAD leader
TMC vs TMC: Mamata-led faction submits affidavits to EC, accuses rival group of forgery
Historic Virginia school for Black children reopens as museum after $6.2m restoration
stories.summary: The historic Union Street School in Leesburg, Virginia has reopened as a museum and community centre. After a refurbishment costing around $6.2 million, the building now serves to educate about Black history. Initially established in 1884, it provided education to Black children during segregation until 1958. The new museum aims to preserve memories and share the stories of those associated with the school.

stories.title: Beavers reintroduced to an English estate changed its stream within a year
stories.summary: The Spains Hall Estate in Essex has welcomed the return of beavers, leading to remarkable improvements in the local ecosystem. A year after their reintroduction, studies revealed an increase in both the quantity and diversity of terrestrial invertebrates. Additionally, water quality enhancements were noted, with elevated oxygen levels and diminished nitrate concentrations.

stories.title: Archaeologists digging in Beijing have found the first Great Wall remains from the Sui dynasty
stories.summary: Recent archaeological discoveries in Beijing have unearthed remnants of the Great Wall from the Sui Dynasty, revolutionizing our understanding of its historical context. This find emphasizes the wall's role as a military outpost on the northern frontier. Additionally, three ancient wooden boats, dating back approximately 1,800 years, were recovered in Fengtai district, showcasing an early transport network in Beijing and shedding light on the area's trade and defense roles.

stories.title: Kentucky man says agent sold him his own home and pressured him for an extra $85,000
stories.summary: After hiring estate agent Rick Walters to sell his home, Jason Wagner later bought a property from him. Wagner alleges he was coerced into paying an extra $85,000 above their original agreement. The Kentucky Court of Appeals reinstated many of Wagner's claims against Walters and Lenihan Real Estate, allowing him to proceed in a lower court after previous dismissals. The decision emphasized concerns regarding Walters' financial transactions during the sale.

stories.title: 'Very grim picture': Gauhati HC flags 1.16 lakh declared foreigners yet to be apprehended in Assam
NYPD shoots kidnapping suspect dead after van chase on busy highway; no child found
'Who laughs when India is insulted?' Rijiju takes digs at Rahul Gandhi over foreign leader's remarks on democracy
Akhilesh calls Dalits 'damdar', vows to wipe out BJP in UP
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav emphasized the importance of the Dalit community in upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections. He called for the ousting of the BJP government, highlighting the need for social justice. Akhilesh criticized the ruling party's record on Dalit issues, which includes the vandalism of Dr. BR Ambedkar's statues. He promised that a Samajwadi Party government would prioritize rights and education for marginalized communities.

stories.title: From Sonia-Natwar row to Advani's Jinnah remarks: 5 political memoirs that stirred storm
Missouri appeals court voids $1 million in punitive damages against therapist in affair case
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, the Missouri Court of Appeals reinforced a jury's verdict against therapist Craig Politte for professional misconduct, confirming charges of medical negligence, battery, and breaches of the Missouri Merchandising Practices Act. Although the jury's compensation award exceeds $2 million, punitive damages were annulled due to distinctions concerning negligence per se claims.

stories.title: Virginia teen, 14, launches tech initiative, distributes 2,000 refurbished devices and wins Diana Award
stories.summary: At just 14 years old, Chris Qian founded ReTech for Kids, a nonprofit dedicated to bridging the technology gap for students lacking access to digital tools. By refurbishing and distributing second-hand devices, the initiative has empowered under-resourced learners. Over three years, it has engaged more than 100 volunteers and provided 2,000 devices, earning Chris both accolades and the prestigious Diana Award for his extraordinary efforts towards educational equity.

stories.title: First Successful Release: Zoo returns 62 young snakes to wild; another release planned for 2027
stories.summary: In a remarkable conservation effort, 62 San Francisco garter snakes, previously raised in a zoo, have been successfully released into their natural environment. This project stems from the need to ensure the species’ survival, as they were originally taken from the wild. Alongside this, restoration activities are being implemented to enhance their habitat.

stories.title: Punjab Congress sets up panel to vet leaders joining from other parties ahead of 2027 polls
Evening newswrap: Parl winter session likely in 1st week of Dec; India beat New Zealand by 22 runs to clinch ODI series 3-1 & more
Two killed as car fleeing police crashes into Volkswagen in UK; 4 arrested
CRPF withdraws anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh, sent to Manipur
stories.summary: In a significant move, over 1,000 CRPF personnel have been redeployed from Chhattisgarh to Manipur amid escalating security concerns. This marks the initial full withdrawal of a battalion from anti-Naxal duties since the decline of armed Maoism. Previously, stationed in Sukma, this battalion has fought against Left Wing Extremism and conducted de-mining operations.

stories.title: Conservative Majority Victory: Conservatives win 64 seats; gas expansion faces C$13.3bn deficit
stories.summary: In a significant political shift, British Columbia has ushered in a Conservative majority government after a decade dominated by the New Democratic Party. Winning 64 out of 93 seats, the Conservatives plan to place a strong emphasis on expanding liquefied natural gas production to enhance energy policy. However, they face fiscal constraints with potential deficits looming, and the new government will need to balance economic growth with public service demands.

stories.title: Scientists have drawn a treasure map of where fossils of ancient sea life are still to be found
stories.summary: In an exciting development, researchers have pinpointed potential hotspots for fossil discoveries that remain undocumented. Focusing on the Cenozoic Era, celebrated for its rich marine biodiversity, this study seeks to enhance fossil hunting by concentrating efforts on less explored territories. Additionally, revisiting collections from natural history museums could yield new insights into ancient species, reinforcing the pursuit of understanding marine life from the past.

stories.title: Farage says Britain faces 'defencelessness', singles out Russia as top threat
Congress postpones ‘Chalo Delhi’ on Constitution Day, to hold marches across states on Nov 26
‘Chats show no mention of Pulkit’: Convict’s father seeks action in Ankita Bhandari murder case
'100% pure' or just marketing? What the law says about misleading food labels
stories.summary: In India, many food products carry misleading labels, which raises serious concerns regarding consumer safety and protection. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, addresses these issues, yet violations persist frequently. Online grocery shopping has exacerbated these discrepancies, complicating accountability for e-commerce platforms. Consumers are encouraged to document discrepancies, approach grievance officers, and report violations to relevant authorities.

stories.title: Massachusetts man, 85, loses $1M in alleged fake Brazil farmland romance scam
stories.summary: An 85-year-old man sent over $1 million to a woman claiming she needed it for taxes and legal fees. Maria Auxiliadora Rezende allegedly fabricated a story concerning inherited farmland in Brazil. Family members noticed unusual transactions and investigated the situation after voicing concerns. Authorities arrested Rezende and she faces a federal indictment for wire fraud.

stories.title: A Philadelphia wetland damaged by old dikes and dredging is being reconnected to a creek
stories.summary: Restoration efforts have begun in the Henderson Marsh area at the John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge, focusing on the excavation of channels to facilitate better water flow. This initiative not only aims to boost wildlife habitats but also enhances flood resilience for nearby communities like Eastwick. The project's success relies on collaboration among various conservation groups, along with upgraded visitor amenities to attract more nature enthusiasts to the refuge.

stories.title: Illinois family awarded $28M in birth injury lawsuit
stories.summary: Teray Boyd received a $28 million verdict following her child's traumatic birth experience, where brain damage resulted from the medical team's failure to execute an emergency C-section. The infant was delivered in dire condition, suffering from oxygen deprivation during labor. Inspired by her journey, Boyd founded two charities focused on assisting young mothers and children with disabilities, underscoring the vital importance of rigorous medical standards during childbirth.

stories.title: Ebro Ahmed Day: Ahmed stopped runaway bus; 19 schoolchildren escaped injury
stories.summary: When Ebro Ahmed spotted a school bus rolling with its door ajar and a driver incapacitated, his instincts kicked in. He quickly jumped aboard and halted the vehicle, safeguarding 19 young lives. The driver was promptly taken to the hospital and is recovering well. For his bravery, Ahmed was honored with accolades, including a dedicated day in St. Paul.

stories.title: A Berkeley scientist spent more than a decade listening to zebra finches
stories.summary: Dr. Julie Elie has meticulously created an acoustic dictionary showcasing zebra finch calls, categorizing 11 distinct vocalization types. Her groundbreaking research suggests that these birds actively comprehend the meanings of their calls, indicating that zebra finches employ a nuanced communication method. This could revolutionize human perspectives on interspecies dialogue, promoting reciprocal understanding. Nevertheless, fully unraveling avian communication remains a complex, ongoing research endeavor for many scientists.

stories.title: Redrawing Pak: Ministers back 12-province plan but pol, constitutional hurdles remain
stories.summary: Pakistan is considering expanding its administrative framework by increasing its provinces from four to twelve, aiming for more efficient governance. Senior officials argue that smaller provinces could enhance public service delivery. Yet, this ambitious initiative faces political hurdles and requires unity among major parties. Redefining boundaries will necessitate constitutional amendments, and a potential referendum may follow, pending parliamentary consent.

stories.title: Yogi targets ‘chaacha-bhatija’, says SP-era jobs came through bribes and recommendations
Iran speaker says Tehran will not accept ‘neither war nor peace’ situation, sets conditions for US deal
'Glory to Mother Chhathi!' PM Modi wishes 'renewed awareness and vitality' for all
'CBI probe into Ajit Pawar's death, name Pune Ring Road after him,' Rohit Pawar urges Amit Shah
DK Shivakumar says proposal to induct woman minister in Karnataka cabinet placed before Congress high command
Spain’s Canary Islands record highest daily migrant arrivals since 2020; 1,488 rescued
Parliament winter session likely in 1st week of December; delimitation bill to be in focus
IndiGo Guwahati-bound flight returns safely to Pune after landing gear fails to retract
stories.summary: An IndiGo Airbus A320 encountered a landing gear malfunction shortly after departing from Pune. Prioritizing safety, the flight returned to Pune International Airport. After approximately two hours of holding to deplete fuel and assess the gear, the aircraft landed without incident. To ensure minimal disruption, IndiGo arranged an alternate flight for the passengers, reinforcing the airline's commitment to their safety and comfort in challenging situations.

stories.title: 'Congress hates tribal heroes': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi for skipping Birsa Munda tribute ceremony
Major accident averted as empty Vande Bharat travels 463 km with faulty brakes
Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary greets devotees as millions prepare to observe Chhath
stories.summary: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary extended greetings for the Sandhya Arghya as Chhath Puja commenced. Many devotees are expected to participate in offering 'arghya' to the setting sun across the state. Safety arrangements involve deploying disaster response teams and local volunteers at various ghats. The festival will conclude with prayers to the rising sun on the following day.

stories.title: 'You brought them in dumper truck': J&K BJP MLA's emotional outburst over handling of slain SPOs' bodies
stories.summary: BJP MLA Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the alleged disrespectful handling of two slain Special Police Officers' bodies, claiming they were transported in a dumper truck. She questioned the delay in addressing their families' concerns, saying officials acted only after intervention from the Lieutenant Governor. The bodies of Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, were recovered from Kishtwar forests on Thursday, with bullet injuries, after they went missing on November 10.

stories.title: ‘Abandoned tribals to Naxal violence’: PM Modi takes aim at previous govts
Congo Ebola outbreak claims nearly half of infected as cases cross 11,000
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 11,000 cases and high fatalities. Basic health measures are inadequate, with most cases detected outside surveillance systems. Children are particularly affected, contributing to rising death rates due to lack of care. Attacks on health workers and facilities have further complicated containment efforts.

stories.title: ‘Utterly ridiculous take’: US official rejects report claiming Quad is on ‘life support’ under Trump
stories.summary: The United States has dismissed a media report suggesting the Quad alliance is struggling under the Trump administration. Senior State Department official Dylan Johnson called the assessment utterly ridiculous and highlighted regular diplomatic engagements among the four countries. A potential leaders' summit in Manila is set to be formalized during upcoming ASEAN meetings.

stories.title: Chicago photographer's $220 thrift store paintings sell for $135,000 after rare discovery
stories.summary: In an unexpected twist of fate, a photographer from Chicago stumbled upon two remarkable original pieces by Warner Sallman in a thrift store back in 2016. After investing $220 for them, his diligence paid off two years later when he sold the artworks to author Jerry Jenkins for an impressive $135,000, reshaping the market landscape for Sallman’s creations and showcasing the hidden treasures often overlooked in thrift shops.

stories.title: Hungarian investigators found $19.5 million in cash buried in forests and hidden in buildings while probing allegations against a former minister

stories.title: India opposes UN call for death penalty moratorium, says no global consensus

Researchers highlighted that the infant's condition did not result in unusual treatment in life or death. This discovery emphasizes the historical presence of congenital differences in human populations.

stories.summary: Urbanization is significantly impacting the habitats of Carnaby's cockatoos in Western Australia. stories.summary: The FAA has lifted the nationwide ground stop caused by a communications failure affecting air traffic control. stories.summary: Next week, US President Donald Trump will engage with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit, despite claims regarding businesswoman Alice Huang and her connection to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surfacing in the media. stories.title: Texas brothers convicted in $240 million cattle investment fraud targeting 2,200 investors
stories.summary: Convicted of a fraudulent cattle investment scheme, Joshua and Jason Link swindled over 2,200 investors, misleading them into thinking their money was turning into cattle purchases. Their actions resulted in colossal financial damages, as they raised more than $240 million through non-existent contracts. Investigations uncovered that funds were misused for personal luxuries rather than fulfilling their financial promises to investors.

stories.title: Rob Roy MacGregor’s gravestone;scans suggest first carvings were made 1,000years before he died
stories.summary: A recent study has uncovered that the gravestone of Rob Roy MacGregor, found at Balquhidder Parish Church, has roots that stretch back an astonishing thousand years prior to his life. It was determined that the delivery van driver failed to check for oncoming vehicles before merging into Bolandis's lane, leading to the collision. The court ruled decisively that Bolandis was not speeding, emphasizing the responsibility of all drivers to prioritize safety when entering traffic.

stories.title: A 13-inch sculpture model that Barbara Hepworth gave her doctor has resurfaced for auction in Cornwall, where the aluminium-and-string study for her famous Winged Figure could fetch as much as £80,000
stories.summary: Barbara Hepworth's miniature sculpture of Winged Figure, a personal gift to Dr. Roger Slack, is returning to auction. This 13-inch artwork could reach an estimated value of £80,000 at the auction in Cornwall. Roger Slack's relationship with Hepworth grew out of their doctor-patient dynamic within the arts community in St Ives. The sculpture reflects Hepworth's artistic legacy and her significant public work on Oxford Street.

stories.summary: A foreclosure dispute surrounding Mamadou Diallo is back in court due to notification concerns. The Ohio appeals court has ruled that Diallo's subsequent actions do not establish proof of proper service for the foreclosure notice. Having been convicted for the murder of his spouse, Diallo contested the foreclosure judgment on the grounds of claimed service deficiencies.

stories.title: Teens raised by strict, obey-without-question parents tend to hold more antisocial beliefs, a US study found, and they also showed small rises in anxiety and depression
stories.summary: Authoritarian parenting can lead to persistent antisocial thoughts among teenagers, affecting their social behavior and emotional well-being. Research indicates that strict parenting fosters beliefs that may justify rule-breaking and aggression. While not all adolescents display increased anxiety or depression, some experience heightened symptoms over time. These findings suggest that parenting styles significantly impact adolescent development and understanding of social norms.

This case serves as a critical reminder of the complexities surrounding title transfers and their legal repercussions in vehicle ownership.

stories.title: Most people dislike coffee at first and learn to love it, and scientists now say the reason may be a slow dopamine signal from the gut that teaches the brain to like flavours linked with calories, even bitter ones
stories.summary: Researchers have discovered that our tastes for certain foods, even those that might initially be bitter, shift as we grow. The gut sends vital signals to our brain about what we eat, influencing our cravings through dopamine, which is known for its role in reward and motivation. Consequently, this insight provides a fascinating explanation for why we often learn to appreciate flavors such as coffee.

stories.summary: A Texas appeals court has dissolved an order barring a granddaughter from coming within 500 feet of family trust property. The court found that the lower court had failed to set a trial date and specify the required security amount. However, the wider dispute over control of the Barbara Tolbert Revocable Trust and the family's inheritance claims remains unresolved.

stories.title: Swiss surgeon reclaims Guinness record with 3,200 heart-shaped objects after losing it in 2024
stories.summary: Diana Reser, a renowned Swiss heart surgeon, proudly holds the record for the largest collection of heart-shaped artifacts, now boasting 3,200 pieces. Her passion began during her medical studies, spurred by thoughtful gifts from loved ones. Reser's eclectic assortment features both decorative items and functional accessories, while she actively champions heart health awareness. Currently, she's on the lookout for a unique heart-shaped shower head to enhance her collection.

stories.title: Stable Oxoboranes Isolated: Würzburg PhD pair trap rare bond; accident unlocks new chemistry
stories.summary: Two doctoral students at the University of Würzburg discovered stable oxoboranes, which contain a triple bond between boron and oxygen. Their findings emerged while studying reactions with diboracumulene and ketones, producing unexpected yellow and orange solids. The three new compounds can be isolated as crystalline solids and remain stable at room temperature. This breakthrough may allow greater exploration of their properties and reactions beyond previous limitations.

Marco Rubio spent over $1.2m in taxpayer-funded flights to attend son's college games
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is facing scrutiny over his frequent trips to Florida to watch his son play college football, with a Washington Post investigation estimating that 23 military aircraft journeys cost taxpayers more than $1.2 million. While Rubio is required to use government aircraft for security reasons, the frequency of his personal trips has raised questions about taxpayer spending and official accountability.

Australian activists ordered to destroy abattoir footage despite retaining copyright
stories.summary: Australia’s High Court has concluded that Farm Transparency International maintains copyright over clandestinely acquired footage, underscoring the ramifications of trespassing despite its public interest nature. Activists are compelled to dispose of the recordings, although third parties may share them legally. This landmark judgment will influence future activism and the interplay of copyright law, prompting legal experts to scrutinize the ramifications for the rights of undercover filming.

stories.title: Australia's High Court overturns $1.346 million abuse compensation award, orders new tria
stories.summary: Australia’s High Court has ordered a retrial in the case concerning the estate of a convicted sexual abuser. The retrial is necessary after the first trial did not adequately address key pieces of evidence. The court clarified important legal principles related to unrepresented litigants and trial procedures. MTH, the survivor, is once again pursuing damages for the abuse she suffered while in foster care.

stories.title: Three school colleagues receive awards for saving cyclist in cardiac arrest
stories.summary: Kip Knowles collapsed in cardiac arrest while cycling alone, and three school staff members intervened promptly. PE teacher Stacey Charman, cookery teacher Chellie Messenger, and school nurse Claire Agnew performed CPR for 25 minutes. Their actions, which included using a defibrillator, revived Kip before medical help arrived. Kip’s wife nominated the trio for awards from St John Ambulance for their lifesaving efforts.

stories.title: A Florida chimpanzee sanctuary cut off by flooding; uses drone to deliver food to a stranded chimp
stories.summary: A chimpanzee named Kaleb faced isolation during heavy flooding at Save the Chimps sanctuary. Staff utilized a drone to deliver essential food and blankets to him safely. The floodwaters disrupted normal delivery routes, which required creative solutions to ensure animal welfare. By using trucks and a drone, caregivers managed to keep the animals fed and healthy, despite the challenges.

Mark Wahlberg's charity marks 25 years, distributing nearly $20m to help disadvantaged children
stories.summary: In 2001, Mark Wahlberg and Jim Wahlberg established the Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation with a mission to uplift disadvantaged youth. Since its inception, the foundation has raised nearly $20 million, funding essential initiatives like summer camps, educational resources, and community recreation spaces. By partnering with various organizations, they strive to enhance the quality of life for children, focusing on health awareness and providing crucial support for families in need.

stories.title: Tennessee county to pay $1 million to veteran Tasered by deputy in 2022
stories.summary: Knox County, Tennessee, has agreed to pay $1 million to Brian Eugene Hux, a 64-year-old disabled Air Force veteran who suffered a fractured skull and brain bleed after being Tasered by a deputy in 2022. The settlement follows a federal appeals court ruling that denied the deputy qualified immunity.

Despite presenting 1,385 pages of evidence to contest her insurer's damage estimate of $440,092, the Fifth Circuit upheld the previous court's decision, highlighting the obstacles homeowners encounter in insurance disputes and concluding her quest for a fairer compensation.

stories.title: Texas businessman loses home ownership battle despite presenting evidence of a $287K bank transfer
stories.summary: A legal battle came to an end for a Texas entrepreneur who aimed to claim ownership of a property. The appellate court upheld the original ruling, stating that the evidence presented was inadequate to support a resulting trust. The testimony regarding a large bank transaction fell short of validating ownership, and the strict probate regulations limited the ability to appeal. Consequently, Karrie Peterson's estate retains the property.

stories.title: Russian imperial family's 197-carat sapphire sells for $4.9 million, beating estimate
stories.summary: In Geneva, a remarkable 197.80-carat gemstone, the Romanov Sapphire from the Russian Crown Jewels, fetched an impressive $4.9 million. This piece of history, once worn by Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna, encapsulates the grandeur of imperial Russia. Following its anonymous sale by the Soviets, the gem's fascinating story has garnered the attention of collectors, underscoring the rising demand for items rich in historical significance.

The Nvidia board swiftly acknowledged Huang's significant contributions while confirming his departure. Consequently, Nvidia experienced a substantial stock decline. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the company begins its search for a permanent replacement.

Companies linked to her invested in DeepSeek to secure Nvidia's Blackwell chips, which are crucial for AI operations. In Singapore, she is under investigation for allegedly misleading authorities during inquiries into her business Megaspeed. Authorities have barred her from re-entering Singapore amid these investigations.

Investment in education and training of teachers is crucial to elevate the country’s innovative capacities.

His $3 billion pledge towards education and healthcare initiatives promises to uplift communities, though his arrival has stirred controversies over political sway and increasing living expenses.

stories.title: From fastest passenger ship to world's largest artificial reef: Historic US ocean liner sinks off Florida
stories.summary: The SS United States, once the fastest passenger ship, was sunk in the Gulf of Mexico. This project aimed to create the world’s largest artificial reef for marine life. The vessel's sinking took longer than anticipated due to safety measures during the operation. Now resting about 180 feet underwater, the ship will become a diving destination. Previous failed commercial efforts to repurpose the ship prompted its preservation as a reef.

stories.title: The Australian in Indira's Tihar compound: When Sonia Gandhi carried lunch for Charles Sobhraj's accomplice
stories.summary: On Christmas Day in 1978, Sonia Gandhi brought a homemade lunch to Tihar Jail for her mother-in-law. Indira Gandhi, a former Prime Minister, was imprisoned during a turbulent political period. The meal was extended to include prison guards and a fellow inmate related to a notorious killer. Despite resistance, Sonia felt compelled to keep family traditions alive during this difficult time.

stories.title: Fujairah midnight crash: Several dead after truck hits multiple vehicles
stories.summary: A devastating crash unfolded on Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Road, resulting in numerous casualties and injuries. Swiftly reacting, emergency units from police and ambulance services, along with Civil Defence, rushed to the site. They administered first aid and transported victims to nearby hospitals for essential care. Fujairah Police have initiated an investigation to ascertain the accident's causes, urging the community against spreading false information.

stories.summary: In the quaint town of Monowi, Nebraska, Elsie Eiler juggles her roles as the mayor and lone resident. Despite the solitude, her tavern serves as a vibrant hub for visitors seeking food, drinks, and companionship, fostering connections that transcend Monowi's unique story. With her unwavering commitment, Elsie not only sustains the town’s essential services but also nurtures the ties to nearby communities, ensuring its enduring legacy.

stories.title: Oklahoma court upholds rental ban; homeowner faces $8,528 in fines
stories.summary: The Oklahoma Supreme Court has ruled in favor of a lower court’s decision that addressed a homeowner's unauthorized short-term rental practices. The activities violated community rules enforced by the homeowners’ association, leading to fines of $8,528 and an injunction against such rentals. Testimonies from neighbors highlighted noise issues from large gatherings, leaving the homeowner disheartened and struggling financially after a protracted legal process.

stories.title: Roy Sullivan survived seven lightning strikes in 35 years, earning a Guinness World Record as the man struck most times
stories.summary: Roy Sullivan, renowned for enduring seven lightning strikes during his tenure as a park ranger, faced numerous injuries that captured public intrigue. Despite his best efforts to shy away from storms, fate dealt him an unexpected hand until 1977. His extraordinary narrative, largely without eyewitness accounts, invites skepticism. Sullivan passed away in 1983, leaving behind an unparalleled legacy of lightning survival that remains unmatched.

stories.title: Colorado pizza driver receives $76,000 after delivering wrong order
stories.summary: A Colorado pizza delivery driver caring for her 82-year-old mother has received more than $76,000 through a fundraiser started by a family she once delivered an incorrect order to. Their decision to pray with her was captured on a doorbell camera, and the video later reached millions of viewers.

stories.title: Owaisi, Aazad announce alliance for UP polls; send message to Akhilesh
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Aazad formed an alliance named Samajik Parivartan Morcha. Azad will be the chief ministerial candidate, aiming to unite marginalized communities for greater political representation. The alliance invites other parties, like the Samajwadi Party and Congress, to join in this effort.

stories.summary: Praneeth Menon was elected to the Vermont House of Representatives from the Orleans-Lamoille district. His election was supported by both the Republican and Democratic parties as a joint nominee. The new representative focused on issues such as cost of living, housing affordability, and education during his campaign. Menon has a background in aeronautical engineering and has worked in various sectors including aviation and defense.

Rejected by his mother, bullied by older monkeys and raised with a stuffed toy, Punch is now showing a softer side
stories.summary: Punch, a Japanese macaque, faced a rough start when he was separated from his mother. He found solace in a stuffed orangutan, which offered him companionship during his early struggles. As time progressed, Punch blossomed and has begun socializing with a younger baby macaque. The zookeepers played a pivotal role in helping him adapt and grow, marking his journey from solitude to engagement within the troop.

The doctor who operated on himself: How Soviet surgeon Leonid Rogozov removed his own appendix in Antarctica
stories.summary: In April 1961, surgeon Leonid Rogozov found himself in a dire situation in Antarctica when he developed acute appendicitis. Stranded at a remote Soviet research station, he realized that evacuation was impossible. Demonstrating extraordinary resolve, he performed surgery on himself with local anesthesia, assisted by two colleagues, successfully removing his appendix. This incredible act is celebrated as a significant milestone in the annals of remote medical practice.

stories.title: Arrest In Ghanaian Teen Killing: NYPD nabs 17-year-old over Bronx shooting; family still seeks justice
stories.summary: In a tragic turn of events, a 17-year-old has been arrested linked to the shooting death of Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot while on his way to school in the Bronx last October. The incident has sparked calls for justice from family, civil rights activists, and officials from Ghana.

stories.title: India simplifies visa rules: Categories cut to 9 from 13, application fields reduced by up to 70%
stories.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs is revamping its visa system to improve transparency and efficiency. By significantly reducing the number of visa categories, the application process for foreign nationals becomes more straightforward. An e-visa option continues to be accessible for citizens from 172 countries, promoting travel to India. These adjustments will provide better predictability for medical treatments and extend student visa durations, supporting legitimate travel and business interactions.

stories.title: After 27 years, nurse Karen Barlow retires; memorable moments are parents holding sick children's hands
stories.summary: Karen Barlow marks the end of a remarkable 27-year journey with the Royal Flying Doctor Service in Australia. Her dedication to providing vital medical assistance to those in isolated regions is commendable. Barlow not only offered solace during treacherous medical flights but also fostered strong connections with families in crisis. Among her memorable moments, she met King Charles and Queen Camilla.

stories.title: Researchers recorded three Sistan sand boas in Rajasthan's Sikar district
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking discovery, three Sistan sand boas have been identified in Sikar district, Rajasthan, a first for the nation. Researchers pointed out unique characteristics that set this species apart from the Indian red sand boa. Interestingly, these snakes inhabit urban and agricultural regions, deviating from their usual sand dune habitats.

stories.title: Kulgam CRPF attack: Manhunt intensifies for LeT affiliated terrorist Md Lateef Bhat
stories.summary: Security agencies are intensifying their manhunt for local terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat in the Kulgam area. Suspected in a recent assault on CRPF personnel, Bhat has a notorious reputation for orchestrating Over Ground Worker networks. His connections to several terror incidents have alarmed officials. Previously, he dodged arrest during a confrontation with security forces in Shopian. Local authorities urge citizens to assist in tracking him and the other fugitives.

stories.summary: India has experienced a decline in the climate change performance index, falling from prior high rankings. The country now sits at 28th position due to rising greenhouse gas emissions and energy use. While India has made significant strides in renewable energy, the overall performance remains low. Comparatively, Pakistan, with lower emissions, is ranked just above India at 26th.

stories.title: Pollution's hidden health cost: Dirty air may also raise diabetes risk, global review finds
stories.summary: Recent findings highlight a concerning connection between PM2.5 air pollution and an increased risk of type 2 diabetes, showing that every 10 microgram per cubic meter rise in PM2.5 could boost diabetes risk by 10% to 16%. Notably, South Asian communities, particularly in India and Bangladesh, may face a 9% heightened risk. This underscores the urgency for improved air quality management to mitigate metabolic diseases, although definitive causation remains unestablished.

He also reflected on his 2023 Union Square controversy and discussed expanding his career through his fashion brand, Vivet.

Dhingra's estate, allowing it to withdraw its claims. This decision overturned the trial court's earlier ruling, reinforcing that plaintiffs can withdraw claims before a judgment is reached, despite Malachite's objections regarding its counterclaims.

stories.title: Navi Mumbai India's cleanest city, Indore's domination ends
stories.summary: For the 2025-26 Swachh Survekshan Awards, Navi Mumbai has claimed the esteemed title of the cleanest city. Following closely are Surat and Vijayawada, securing the second and third positions, respectively. Additionally, Rewa from Madhya Pradesh has been honored as the cleanest riverfront town this year. Significant mentions include Rudrapur as the cleanest Himalayan city, along with various award categories highlighting different city populations.

stories.title: Scientists discover uncounted right whale calf off Canada, bringing season's total to 24 amid population of 380
stories.summary: In a remarkable development, scientists have confirmed the sighting of a previously unrecorded North Atlantic right whale calf near Quebec, bringing this season's total to 24, the highest since 2009. Researchers believe the calf's mother, Silt, gave birth in the warmer waters of the southeastern U.S. Despite this positive news, the North Atlantic right whale population remains critically endangered, with an estimated 380 individuals.

Collegium wants transfer of HC judges streamlined, random ways discarded

Currently, transfers are largely subject to personal criteria, which the collegium aims to revise. This new policy emphasizes objective reasoning to streamline the transfer process, reduce personal biases, and enhance accountability regarding judges’ conduct and expertise, marking a pivotal evolution in judicial integrity management.

stories.title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court declared that divorces executed overseas, based on grounds not acknowledged under Indian law, are invalid. This ruling implies that individuals who remarry after such foreign divorces may risk prosecution for bigamy. The court also affirmed that marriages conducted according to Indian traditions hold validity, irrespective of any foreign citizenship.

stories.title: Complete data could've raised average Diwali pollution level in Delhi by 49%
stories.summary: On Diwali night, the absence of PM2.5 data from monitoring stations led to distorted pollution readings in Delhi. Research by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air indicated that pollution levels might have increased by as much as 49%. While the Central Pollution Control Board pointed out calibration limitations, readings from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee were inconsistent.

stories.title: Ohio man challenges $23,161 share after co-owner gets $171,635 from property sale
stories.summary: An Ohio appeals court dismissed a man's challenge to his $23,161 share of property sale proceeds after the money was distributed. However, the court said he could not continue the appeal because he had not obtained a stay on the payment.

The court also denied Sandstrom's petition to change the existing parenting arrangements, emphasizing the need for compliance with court directives regarding parenting time.

stories.summary: The Skechers Pier to Pier Friendship Walk has become an essential event in Southern California's charity scene. In 2026, it achieved a remarkable milestone by raising $3.3 million to aid children with special needs. This annual gathering also plays a crucial role in public education and scholarships, assisting students at all levels. With the Friendship Campus opening in January 2027, support for neurodivergent young adults is set to expand significantly.

stories.title: Study Links Climate And Violence: Peru skeletons show low conflict; ritual sacrifice stays distinct
stories.summary: Throughout history, ancient communities in Peru's Lambayeque Valley confronted significant flooding and food scarcity. Interestingly, despite these hardships, instances of interpersonal violence were notably infrequent. Research indicates that only a tiny percentage of skeletal remains revealed signs of conflict. Instead, these resilient societies cleverly adapted, capitalizing on marine resources to weather environmental challenges.

Continued conservation efforts hold the key to potentially establishing a new haven for short-tailed albatrosses on the island.

Seyfried plans to share her upcoming film 'Steps', which explores complex relationships, showcasing the unique viewpoints children have of their celebrity parents and how those views evolve over time.

stories.summary: Iran revealed a large underground military facility that contains various ballistic and cruise missiles amidst ongoing tensions. Senior military officials warned of potential attacks on American forces if conflicts resume, highlighting Iran's preparedness. Significant political leaders emphasized the need for the US to recognize Iran's conditions to resolve conflicts.

The case has been sent back to the trial court for further proceedings.

Acquired just two years ago from Zedd for $17.125 million, this luxurious property has a rich celebrity lineage, previously owned by Joe Jonas and Sophie Turner. Boasting opulent features such as a recording studio and a private gym, it's yet to be determined if they'll achieve their asking price.

stories.summary: Research indicates that microplastics in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch may be changing ocean color. This change creates a subtle blue-green tint that satellites have detected over twenty years.
